notes: Workshop summary: focused on dedicated sizing for interactive chat + nightly reranking batch. Goal: predictable cost + p95 latency guardrails.
Baseline traffic (from customer traces): steady-state QPS 15-25 during business hours; typical request length 300-700 tokens (median ~420 tokens).
Tokens/sec steady-state estimate: ~18k tokens/sec (steady). Observed short bursts up to 120 QPS for 3-8 minutes (peak tokens/sec ~50k-60k).
Customer latency targets: p95 <= 300ms for chat; p99 <= 1s acceptable for non-critical rerank jobs. Quote from Marco (Eng Lead): "can't afford >500ms p95 during business hours".

Redwood recommendations from workshop: start with reserved pool = 4x NVIDIA H100(80GB) for baseline, allow burst policy to 8x for scheduled peaks; enable continuous batching with max_wait 25ms and dynamic KV prefix caching for common prompts.
Batching/throughput guidance: target 12-16 concurrent inference streams per GPU for chat model variants; use quantized 4-bit model variant for reranking batch to reduce token cost overnight.

SLA asks from customer: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool, p95 latency objectives tied to route (business-hours vs background), financial credits for missed latency SLOs. Legal requests sample SLO language and maintenance windows.
Operational notes: must support EU data residency (primary workspace in eu-west-1), SSO via SAML, central audit logs forwarded to customer's SIEM, customer will manage KMS keys (bring-your-own).

POC scope agreed: 2-week dedicated POC with traffic replay (sanitized), verify p95 latency at steady-state and under 3-minute burst, run cost estimate report, on-call rotation for incident simulation.
